items.description:

1. It is a mixture-of-experts model: 35B parameters in total, but only about 3B wake up at a time (that is the "A3B" in 35B-A3B).

2. That is why OpenBMB says it runs at 13+ tokens a second in just 3 GB of memory on an iPhone 17 Pro Max, with no internet.

The catch: the benchmarks are OpenBMB's own tests. The 3 GB phone figure is OpenBMB's own on-device runtime, not the Ollama download, and their iPhone app page recommends a 12 GB phone and about 17 GB of free storage for the 35B (you build that app yourself in Xcode).

👇 READ BELOW for how it works:

1. Ask Claude to fix one thing and it quietly changes twenty others. A couple days later your app breaks and you have no clue which edit did it.

2. The bouncer sits in front of Claude. Before Claude touches anything, it hands the bouncer a list of exactly what it plans to change.

3. The bouncer checks every item on that list against what you actually asked for.

4. The item you asked for gets a tick and goes in. Every random extra change gets a cross and never gets made.

5. So you never find surprise edits that break your app days later.

Try it on a small fix first, like a login button: you'll see the extras get thrown out before they ever touch your code.

Why it matters: Claude is fast, but it will happily edit things you never mentioned. This keeps its speed and keeps your code yours.
